content.intro: This lesson covers model evaluation before and after fine-tuning through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Customize an existing model only after establishing a baseline and deciding prompting or retrieval is insufficient. Dataset permissions, compute, evaluation, and versioned artifacts all matter.

items.title: Measuring task performance
items.text: Use measuring task performance to reason about behavior under real workloads, not just a successful local example. Measure latency and cost on representative requests, define operational limits and rollback options, and test what happens when dependencies slow down or fail.

items.title: Comparing quality, cost, and latency
items.text: Use comparing quality, cost, and latency to turn a vague quality claim into an observable criterion. Define a representative dataset, an expected outcome or rubric, a baseline, and the failure categories you will record; interpret aggregate scores alongside examples and affected groups.

items.title: Safety regression testing
items.text: Safety regression testing is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
